text:
Sam J: Heads-up — Acme reports repeated 503/504s hitting hosted inference since 09:10 PST. They say SDK retries are looping and they saw duplicate billing for the same user session. Repro steps below and logs attached.
Sam J: Repro (from customer's SDK):
```bash
# single request they run repeatedly
redwood.generate({ model: 'rwd-14b', input: 'summarize: ...', timeout: 120000 })
# client shows 504 then immediate retry
```
Sam J: Customer logs:
```text
[2026-03-17T09:10:02Z] WARN request failed status=504 id=abc123
[2026-03-17T09:10:02Z] INFO retrying attempt=1
[2026-03-17T09:10:05Z] WARN request failed status=504 id=abc124
```
Sam J: They also pasted an edge gateway snippet showing many ECONNRESET and keepalive timeouts. URL: https://acme.example/repro
Alex R: Thanks, looking. Do we have a request id or trace? can someone paste the p95/99 for gateway->runtime at 09:05-09:15? :mag:
Sam J: Customer request_id=abc123, trace header x-rwd-trace=tr-9f2. They see the SDK doing an immediate retry (no jitter) on 504.
Maria P: eng-oncall here. I pulled traces for tr-9f2 — the gateway shows a slow write to runtime (socket write stalled ~3s) and then the ingress returned 504. Upstream runtime accepted the connection but did not ack due to a blocking GC on the model runner (we have a flagged host with older driver). Kicking off more logs now.
eng-oncall: Paging runtime team: suspected host-level stall + auth fanout spike. Can runtime team confirm if any model worker was OOM/GC during that period? @runtime-bot can you show worker metrics for host=gw-rt-07 from 09:00-09:20?
runtime-bot: metrics snapshot: host=gw-rt-07 cpu=92% mem=78% gc-pauses=2 x 1.8s, active-requests=48, q-length=12, kvcache-locks=3
Alex R: That gc pause + queue looks suspicious. With active-requests=48 our batching could have amplified tail latency. Also seeing token-prefetching disabled for that model -> more per-request work.
Sam J: Customer also says they saw 502 once, then dozens of 504s. Their SDK retry policy is exponential backoff disabled (default misconfigured). They reported double-billing because retries completed and were billed twice by our usage meter.
Maria P: Action items: 1) Temporarily route Acme to another runtime pool (canary) 2) Push an emergency config to re-enable token-prefetching/shorter batch window for rwd-14b 3) Add a short client-side guidance note about backoff.
Alex R: I'll open a routing override now for tenant=acme -> pool=dedicated-canary-usw2. Applying ACL and warm pool. ETA ~2m. Will post when done.
eng-oncall: Also flipping an ingress timeout guard for streaming endpoints to drop long-hung writes earlier (adjust from 30s -> 8s) as a mitigation to prevent cascading retries.
runtime-bot: Routing override applied for tenant=acme -> dedicated-canary-usw2 (id=ro-778). Pool warm: 6/8 nodes ready.
Sam J: Thanks. Can we confirm billing dedup window? We need to credit Acme for any double-counted tokens in the spike. What logs do we need from billing? @Support Bot, can you open a billing ticket?
Support Bot: Created billing ticket BLG-2026-112 referencing request_ids [abc123, abc124] and tenant acme. Assigned to @Finance Ops.
Maria P: For postmortem: track root cause = host-level GC + high q-length causing slow writes + non-robust client retry config. Short-term mitigations done. Next steps: runtime upgrade to newer driver on gw-rt-07, enforce default SDK backoff (>=500ms jittered), and add billing dedupe logic for identical trace ids within a 10s window.
Alex R: Noted. I'll follow up when the driver upgrade completes. Also pinging Customer Success for comms draft.
Sam J: I'll send Acme a status update: "we routed you to a warmed pool and disabled the hung worker; we're reviewing billing and will compensate any duplicated usage." Will post copy here.
Sam J: Draft to Acme:
> Hey team — we've routed your traffic away from a degraded host and applied mitigations. We're investigating billing duplicates and will refund any double-charged tokens. We'll follow up with timeline within 24 hours.
Maria P: Good. Closing thread for now, reopen if 5xx pattern returns after routing. :white_check_mark:
